lesson_title: Guided practice B: critique and revision
essential_question: How can understanding artistic voice and advanced composition help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?

task_brief: Day 6 of "Artistic Voice and Advanced Composition" (unit 1, grade 8) is a guided practice (second pass) on critique and revision. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 40–60 minutes. The unit is working toward: Develop a coherent visual series with an artist statement and process evidence. Today's work contributes to that by handling critique and revision at the guided practice b stage, against the unit's wider topics of personal artistic questions, composition and visual hierarchy, symbol metaphor and abstraction, and style studies without copying. This session produces reviewable evidence toward the unit performance task.
primary_task: Complete a second supported pass on critique and revision with the reference put away. Make two fresh short studies from memory and judgement, then set them beside the first pass. Where the unassisted work differs, decide which version better achieves the effect and write the reason in terms of the actual work, not preference alone. Revisit the move you flagged as unrepeatable and report honestly whether it held. Sharing remains private; no recording, photograph, or performance for an audience is required. Use the attached earlier-pass substitute when prior work is unavailable, hide it as directed, and finish both unassisted studies before checking. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about critique and revision, and it belongs to "Artistic Voice and Advanced Composition", which also covers separate topics such as personal artistic questions. Close out with this check before you stop: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about critique and revision; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. At grade 8 the bar is independent work that anticipates the obvious objection: name the case most likely to break your result, test it, and report what happened.
requirements: Meet this lesson's own success criteria: The learner completes the central task about critique and revision., The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer., and The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
Address the lesson objective: Practice critique and revision with prompts, feedback, and gradually reduced support.
Produce the deliverable for a guided practice (second pass): Two unassisted studies, a reasoned comparison against the first pass, and a verdict on the previously flagged move.
Show the process, not only the result — a working log, draft, or annotated study.
Complete the critique criteria list in this package before submitting.
deliverable: Two unassisted studies, a reasoned comparison against the first pass, and a verdict on the previously flagged move.
guided_scaffold_note: Scaffolding for critique and revision fades within the session: the first case may be worked with the reference, model, or prompts in view, and the second must be attempted before checking anything. The supporting adult may ask "what supports that move?" after a step but should not supply the step. Where the unscaffolded attempt diverges from the scaffolded one, the divergence itself is the thing to examine, not something to erase.

critique_criteria: Two fresh studies were made without the reference in view.
The unassisted work is compared against the first pass with a reasoned verdict on which better achieves the effect.
The previously flagged move is revisited with an honest report of whether it held.
No recording, photograph, performance, or audience was required.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Provide a non-performance or low-audience option when needed without lowering the academic target.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting critique and revision.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for critique and revision follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for critique and revision, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for critique and revision works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of critique and revision, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking critique and revision mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply critique and revision under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on critique and revision rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
